latest.notes:
Stops songs settling into one part of the day.

Same song now reaches four days instead of eight hours. The stepper's step grows with the value — ten minutes near an hour, six hours past a day — and it reads '45 min', '3 hr 30 min', '2 days'.

The same-time-of-day window is now adjustable in Settings ▸ Scheduling ▸ Dayparting. It has always been a real setting with a 90-minute default, but its only control lived in a screen nothing navigated to, so it could never be changed.

Cross-day churn — keeping a song out of a clock hour it holds on a nearby day — is no longer the first rule abandoned when a rotation is tight. It now outlives same-artist separation, because two songs by one artist twenty minutes apart is a smaller sin than a song parked in the same hour every day.

And both daypart rules now report how often they had to yield, as a proportion of the day's songs. If your station sounds the same at the same time each day, that number is the one to watch — and the rotation lines in the same report say how many songs it would take to fix.
